MANAGEMENT OF MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION: STEMI 
TIME IS MUSCLE – do not delay reperfusion 
DOOR TO NEEDLE TIME £ 30 MINUTES 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
STEMI 
* ST Elevation in 2 or more contiguous leads  
  (see box for criteria) 
* New LBBB or presumably  
  new LBBB (see Sgarbossa's criteria) 
* True posterior MI: tall R in V1 & STE ≥ 0.5mm in V7-9  
* RV infarction: ST elevation V4R  
ST SEGMENT CRITERIA STEMI 
ST elevation in 2 or more contiguous leads 
* J-point elevation in men ≥ 40 years old 
    - 2mm in leads V2 and V3 
    - 1mm in all other leads 
* J-point elevation in men < 40 years old 
    - 2.5mm in leads V2 and V3 
    - 1mm in all other leads 
* J-point elevation in women 
    - 1.5mm in leads V2 and V3 
    - 1mm in all other leads 
CONSIDER 
AORTIC DISSECTION 
* Central chest pain radiating to   
   back - tearing sensation 
* Differential radial pulse 
* Differential arm BP > 15 mmHg 
* Widened mediastinum on CXR (> 8cm) 
Start Adjunctive Treatments 
* Heparin 
   LMWH:  Clexane® 30mg IV stat then 1mg/kg SC after 15 min 
                                             or if no LMWH 
   Heparin: 60IU/kg (max 4000IU) IV stat then infusion with 12IU/kg/hr  
                                           (max 1000IU/hr) 
 
* Thienopyridines 
   Clopidogrel (Plavix®) 300mg stat po 
 
* Statin 
   Simvastatin (Zocor®) 40mg stat po 
 
* β blocker (if no contraindications - see box) 
    Atenolol (Tenormin®) 50mg stat po 
Contraindications 
β Blockers 
* Haemodynamic instability 
* Heart failure 
* Pulmonary oedema 
* SBP < 100 mmHg 
* Bradycardia (HR ≤ 60 bpm)  
* AV block 2° or 3° 
* Asthma  
THROMBOLYSIS 
             - provided no contraindications  (see boxes) 
                - signed consent 
 
* TPA / Alteplase (Actilyse®) 
   15mg IV bolus then 
   0.75mg/kg over 30min (max 50mg) then 
   0.5mg/kg over 60min (max 35mg)     
Maximum total dose - 100mg 
 
OR 
* Streptokinase (Streptase®) 
  1.5MU in 200ml N/S over 1hr 
 
 
 
      OR 
* Tenectaplase (Metalyse®) 
   1. Late patient presenation ³ 10 hrs post pain onset 
   2. Allergy to Streptokinase 
 
   Weight < 100 kg –  8 000 IU IV over 10 seconds 
  Weight >  100 kg – 10 000 IU IV over 10 seconds 
Time of onset of symptoms £ 12 hours? 
Still continuous 
chest pain? 
YES 
NO 
NO 
Refer to cardiology 
* Refer to cardiology  
* Consider Nitroglycerin infusion             
   (provided no contraindications)  
YES 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020 
Contents

     
SGARBOSSA CRITERIA 
LBBB or PACED RHYTHM 
* Criteria A (5 points) 
   ≥ 1mm of concordant ST elevation in at least one lead   
* Criteria B (3 points) 
   ≥ 1mm of concordant ST depression in lead V1,V2 or V3  
* Criteria C (2 points) 
   ≥ 5mm of discordant ST elevation in at least one lead 
 
A total score of ≥ 3 has a specificity of 90% for 
diagnosing myocardial infarction 
Absolute Contraindications Thrombolysis 
* Any prior intracranial haemorrhage 
* Known structural cerebral vascular lesion e.g.
